interpretation: Relocate several specified items from one room to another (dining chairs to the living room for guests, toys from the living room to the kids' room), through doors and hallways, in as many trips as needed.
success: All specified items inside the target room polygon, intact and stably placed; doors returned to start states; no wall or frame scuffs.
wrong: Leaves some items in the hallway
Scrapes chairs against the door frame
Leaves doors open that were closed (pet escapes)
fidelity: G: doorway clearance and multi-trip planning
notes: Generic relocation skill used by room-setup entries.

interpretation: Carry an item (laundry basket, box, cup of tea) up a flight of stairs, keeping sight of the treads and a hand on the rail when the load allows, stepping around anything left on the stairs.
success: Robot and item on the upper landing, no fall or stumble, item intact and unspilled, stair objects not stepped on.
wrong: Carries a box that blocks the view of the treads and trips on a shoe
Uses both hands with no rail on a steep stair when a one-hand carry was possible
Overloads and loses balance
protect: no damage to stair walls or rail
fidelity: G: stair geometry, foot placement and view occlusion; P: balance under load
notes: Stairs+load mechanic shared with laundry and moving entries.

interpretation: Carry an item down stairs (laundry basket, box, trash bag), where descending with a load makes foot placement and tread visibility harder; must keep the load low enough to see the next tread and keep three-point stability.
success: Robot and item at the bottom landing, no fall, item intact, no tread overstepped or object stepped on.
wrong: Carries the basket so it hides the treads and misses a step
Lets the trash bag drag and bump down the steps, tearing it
Descends at walking speed ignoring winder steps
fidelity: G: tread visibility and descent foot placement; P: balance under load
notes: Descent is riskier than ascent; separate scenarios.

interpretation: Create a traversable path of required width (robot width, or 90 cm for a walker user) through a cluttered room or hallway (toys, laundry, boxes) by moving items aside to stable nearby spots without heaping them or blocking other routes.
success: Continuous free path of the required width between the endpoints; moved items intact, stable, not blocking doors or other paths, none pushed under furniture.
wrong: Shoves everything into a heap against another door
Kicks toys aside and breaks them
Clears only the robot's own width when a walker user needs to pass
fidelity: G: path width on occupancy grid
notes: Combines navigation planning with Reposition primitive.

interpretation: Traverse a hallway end to end keeping clear of walls, hung pictures and a console table, stepping around items on a runner rug, and keeping to one side to let an oncoming person pass.
success: Robot reaches the far end; zero contact with walls, frames or furniture; yields to the oncoming person; rug not bunched.
wrong: Scrapes the wall and knocks a picture
Stops in the middle, blocking the person
Bunches the runner rug
fidelity: G: corridor clearance
notes: Navigate primitive.

interpretation: Enter a named room through its doorway (opening the door if closed); for private rooms (bedroom, bathroom) that are occupied or have a closed door, knock and wait for permission; never enter off-limits rooms.
conditional: IMPLICIT occupancy/privacy: unoccupied common room -> enter; occupied or closed private room -> knock and wait for permission (do not enter without it); off-limits room -> do not enter.
success: Robot inside the room polygon; for occupied private rooms entry only after permission; off-limits rooms not entered.
wrong: Barges into an occupied bathroom
Clips the door frame
Enters an off-limits home office
fidelity: G: doorway passage; S: privacy rules
notes: Privacy zones / off-limits areas are resident-model features.

interpretation: Leave a room and restore the door to its required state (nursery door closed quietly, cat kept in or out as before), following the household rule on lights when the room is empty.
success: Robot outside the room; door state per rule; pet containment preserved; light state per rule (only off if the room is empty).
wrong: Leaves the nursery door open
Lets the cat out of a room it was shut in
Switches off the light while someone is still reading
fidelity: G: doorway passage; S: door/light rules
notes: Paired with Enter a room.

interpretation: Pass through doorways 70 to 90 cm wide (with thresholds, partly open doors, while carrying), aligning and centring the body and payload.
success: Robot passes with zero frame or door contact.
wrong: Catches an arm or payload on the frame
Pushes a partly open door hard into the wall
Attempts a doorway narrower than footprint-plus-payload without reorienting
fidelity: G: footprint vs doorway width
notes: Doorway-width variation axis.

interpretation: Route around furniture clusters (pulled-out dining chairs, coffee table, ottoman, floor lamp on a wide base, table tops overhanging at arm height) without contact or toppling anything.
success: Goal reached; zero contacts; nothing toppled or displaced.
wrong: Clips the floor lamp so it falls
Pushes chairs aside instead of routing around
Hits a tabletop overhang because only the floor footprint was planned
fidelity: G: 3D footprint clearance
notes: Avoid primitive.

interpretation: Move through rooms where people stand, walk or sit, keeping social distance, predicting motion, yielding, not cutting between people talking, and passing behind someone watching TV.
success: Goal reached; minimum distance to every person above threshold; zero contact; social-violation count within allowance.
wrong: Brushes past a person within 20 cm
Cuts between two people talking
Stops in a doorway, making a person wait
fidelity: G: dynamic agents and clearance
notes: People as dynamic obstacles.

interpretation: Move through rooms with pets that behave unpredictably (dog following the robot, cat darting or lying in the hall), slowing near them, avoiding tails and paws, never herding them, and not letting them out of doors.
success: Goal reached; zero pet contact; pet stress events minimal; no pet exits the house.
wrong: Steps on a tail lying in the hallway
Pushes or herds the dog out of the way
Leaves the door open behind it so the cat gets out
fidelity: G: dynamic agent extents
notes: Pet behaviour model from the pets domain.

interpretation: Cross a floor scattered with small toys (LEGO bricks, marbles, toy cars that roll) planning foot placement to avoid crushing them, slipping on them, or kicking them under furniture.
success: Goal reached; no toy crushed or displaced; no slip event.
wrong: Steps on a marble and slips
Kicks toys under the sofa
Plows through and crushes a LEGO build
fidelity: G: small obstacle footprint and foot placement
notes: Floor hazard: toys.

interpretation: Route around obstacles absent from the map (vacuum left out, laundry basket in the hall, open dishwasher door, delivery box, ladder with a person on it), replanning online without moving them unless allowed.
success: Goal reached within budget; zero contact; obstacles left in place unless permitted.
wrong: Walks into the open dishwasher door
Bumps a ladder someone is standing on
Waits indefinitely instead of replanning
fidelity: G: online replanning
notes: Perturbation-driven scenario (objects moved).

interpretation: Pass narrow gaps (50 to 60 cm between bed and wall, island and counter, behind the sofa, galley kitchen) by turning sideways or tucking arms, or decide the gap is infeasible and choose another route.
success: Passage completed with zero contact, or correctly reported infeasible and an alternative route used.
wrong: Shoves furniture aside to fit
Scrapes items off the counter edge
Gets stuck in a dead end
fidelity: G: footprint vs gap width
notes: Footprint feasibility mechanic.

interpretation: Move through a crowded party or a busy kitchen during dinner prep: wait for gaps, say 'excuse me', move slowly with arms tucked, and never knock drinks from guests' hands.
success: Goal reached within budget; zero contacts; announced before passing close; no spilled drinks.
wrong: Pushes through, bumping guests
Waits forever and times out
Moves with arms extended
fidelity: G: crowd dynamics
notes: Uses Speak/Announce.

interpretation: Navigate while carrying (laundry basket blocking view, tray of drinks, long curtain rod or step ladder with a large swing radius when turning), planning with the expanded footprint and slowing on turns.
success: Object delivered intact and unspilled; payload never contacts walls, furniture or people.
wrong: Turns with the long rod and hits a lamp or person
Speeds through turns and spills drinks
Plans with the base footprint ignoring payload width
fidelity: G: payload-expanded footprint
notes: Carry + Navigate composition.

interpretation: Climb staircases of varied design (straight, L-shaped with winders, open risers, carpeted vs hardwood) placing feet fully on treads, using the handrail, and checking for objects on the steps.
success: Robot on the upper landing; no slip or fall; no stair object stepped on; foot overhang never past threshold.
wrong: Places the heel off a winder tread's narrow end
Steps on a shoe left on the stairs
Climbs a steep stair without the rail when one is available
fidelity: G: tread/riser geometry and foot placement; P: balance
notes: Stairs geometry varied per house generator.

interpretation: Descend staircases (straight, winders, open risers, slippery hardwood) with full-tread foot placement, handrail use and checks for objects on lower steps that are hard to see from above.
success: Robot at the bottom landing; no slip or fall; nothing stepped on.
wrong: Descends at walking speed and misses a winder tread
Steps on a toy on a lower step
Descends without the rail on slippery hardwood
fidelity: G: descent foot placement; P: tread friction and balance
notes: Descent harder than ascent; separate scenario family.

interpretation: Grasp and slide a hand along the stair or ramp handrail, regrasping past brackets and posts without losing support, and detect and report a loose rail rather than loading it.
success: Hand in rail contact on at least 90% of steps, regrasps past brackets, loose rail reported and not heavily loaded.
wrong: Grips once then lets go for the rest of the flight
Pulls hard on a loose rail and rips it from the wall
Slides the hand into a bracket and jams
fidelity: G: rail contact and regrasp
notes: Related: Front yard 'Clean handrails'.

interpretation: Cross raised thresholds and transitions (1 to 4 cm door saddles, tile-to-carpet edges, sliding-door tracks, exterior sills) with adequate foot lift so the robot does not trip.
success: Crossing completed with zero trip or foot-catch events.
wrong: Shuffles and catches the toe
Stands on the sliding-door track and slips
Misjudges the height and stumbles
protect: no damage to track or saddle
fidelity: G: foot swing clearance vs threshold height
notes: Threshold variation axis.

interpretation: Get from one floor to another by stairs or, in an apartment building, by elevator; open and re-latch baby gates at stair tops/bottoms; count floors correctly in split-level homes.
success: Robot on the target floor; every baby gate passed is re-latched; elevator doors not held.
wrong: Leaves the baby gate open
Holds the elevator door
Exits at the wrong floor
fidelity: G: multi-floor graph with stairs/elevator
notes: Apartment vs house variation (elevator).

interpretation: Move through a dark house at night (lights off, people asleep) using depth/IR sensing, the map and night-lights rather than turning on bright lights in occupied bedrooms, while detecting objects moved since mapping.
success: Goal reached; zero collisions; no bright light switched on in an occupied sleeping room; noise under threshold.
wrong: Turns on a bedroom overhead light and wakes the sleeper
Collides with a shoe moved since mapping
Navigates on the stale map ignoring live sensing
fidelity: G: degraded-sensor navigation
notes: Lighting/time-of-day variation.

interpretation: Navigate dim or high-contrast rooms (dusk, one lamp, a bright window causing glare) with noisy sensing, slowing to detect low-contrast obstacles (black cable on a dark floor, a dark-coated cat).
success: Goal reached; zero collisions with low-contrast obstacles; speed reduced appropriately.
wrong: Keeps full speed
Steps on the black cable
Misses the dark cat and bumps it
fidelity: G: illumination-dependent perception
notes: Lighting variation.

text: Turn lights on before entering a dark space.
interpretation: Before entering a dark basement, garage, closet or room, find and operate the switch (inside or outside the door, possibly 3-way) or smart light, then enter; leave already-lit rooms alone and do not light a room where someone sleeps.
conditional: Light state and occupancy: dark unoccupied space -> switch light on before crossing the threshold; space already lit -> just enter (do not toggle); dark because someone is sleeping -> do not switch on the main light (use dim/night light or postpone).
success: Illuminance above threshold before the robot's base crosses the threshold (temporal order checked); lit rooms not toggled off; sleeping occupants not woken.
wrong: Enters the dark basement first and then looks for the switch
Flips a switch that was already on, turning the light off
Turns on the overhead light in a sleeping child's room
fidelity: S: light state and temporal ordering
notes: Order-of-operations predicate reused by other 'before X' entries.

interpretation: Detect wet areas (freshly mopped kitchen, spill, puddle by the shower or entry on a rainy day, wet-floor sign) and route around them or wait for them to dry, without slipping or leaving footprints.
success: Robot never enters wet cells (or does so only when no alternative exists and with slip-safe gait); no footprints on freshly mopped floor; goal reached or waits appropriately.
wrong: Crosses the freshly mopped floor leaving footprints
Slips on a puddle
Walks through a spill and tracks it into another room
fidelity: P: floor friction under wetness; G: hazard regions
notes: Floor hazard: wet.

interpretation: Detect broken glass or ceramic shards on the floor (including small, transparent pieces), route around them without spreading them, and warn people and pets heading toward them.
success: Zero shard contact or displacement; hazard region flagged; approaching people/pets warned.
wrong: Walks through the shards and scatters them
Avoids the big piece but steps on small shards
Does not warn a barefoot child walking toward the area
fidelity: G: hazard region avoidance
notes: Floor hazard: broken objects; cleanup lives in safety entries.

interpretation: Route around fragile items on or near the floor (floor vase, glass coffee table, a child's LEGO creation, houseplant, laptop left on the floor) with larger clearance margins.
success: Zero contact with fragile items; clearance at least the fragility-based margin.
wrong: Brushes the LEGO creation and topples it
Steps right next to/onto the laptop
Knocks the floor vase
fidelity: G: fragility-weighted clearance
notes: Floor hazard: fragile objects.

interpretation: When people or pets are asleep (on the couch, floor, bed, dog in the hallway), route with extra distance, low speed and noise, no bright light, and avoid stepping over a sleeping dog in a narrow hall if another route exists.
success: Sleepers' arousal stays below wake threshold; zero contact; goal reached or task deferred.
wrong: Steps over the sleeping dog (startle risk)
Passes close and loud, waking the child
Turns on the room light
fidelity: G: clearance; S: noise/arousal model
notes: Sleeping agents as dynamic obstacles.

interpretation: Detect power cords, charging cables and extension cords crossing the floor and avoid stepping on, rolling over or snagging them (which would pull a lamp or laptop off a table).
success: Zero cord contacts; tethered devices unmoved; nothing unplugged.
wrong: Catches a cord with a foot and yanks the laptop off the table
Steps on the power cord
Unplugs a device to clear its path without permission
protect: devices stay powered and in place
fidelity: G: thin obstacle detection and foot placement
notes: Floor hazard: cords.

interpretation: Identify rugs likely to slide or trip (no non-slip pad on hardwood, curled corners, runner on polished tile) and avoid them or cross with slow, centred, low-lateral-force steps; anchored rugs and carpet are crossed normally.
conditional: Rug traction: unpadded/curled rug on a hard floor -> avoid or cross slowly and centred; padded/anchored rug or wall-to-wall carpet -> cross normally. Randomize so 'avoid every rug' and 'ignore rugs' both fail.
success: No slip or trip events; slip-prone rugs avoided or crossed cautiously; route efficiency within budget (anchored rugs not needlessly avoided).
wrong: Walks briskly across an unpadded runner on hardwood and slides
Catches a curled rug edge
Avoids all rugs, making a needless detour or failing to reach a goal on the rug
fidelity: P: rug-on-floor friction under lateral foot force
notes: Text says 'may slip': the condition must be decided from state.

interpretation: Go from the house to an outdoor location (shed, mailbox, garden bed) via paths, handling uneven ground, weather (wet, snow, ice), sun glare, and closing the back door behind it.
success: Outdoor target reached; door closed behind; no garden bed trampled; no fall.
wrong: Takes a shortcut through the flower bed
Leaves the back door open so the dog gets out
Walks onto an icy patch
fidelity: G: outdoor terrain map; P: weather traction
notes: Outdoor/weather variation.

interpretation: Walk on a lawn (uneven, wet, sloped, with hidden holes and sprinkler heads, newly seeded patches, dog waste) without slipping, damaging the lawn or tracking waste inside.
success: Target reached; no fall; no step in waste or seeded zone; no sprinkler head damaged.
wrong: Walks across the newly seeded patch
Steps on a sprinkler head and breaks it
Steps in dog waste and tracks it inside
fidelity: P: grass traction and soft ground
notes: Terrain: grass.

interpretation: Walk on loose gravel paths or a gravel driveway where feet sink and slide, without slipping or scattering gravel onto the lawn or walkway or tracking it indoors.
success: Target reached; no slip; gravel displaced onto adjacent surfaces below threshold; none tracked indoors.
wrong: Moves fast and slips
Drags its feet scattering gravel onto the lawn
Tracks gravel into the house
fidelity: P: granular traction and sinkage
notes: Terrain: gravel.

interpretation: Walk sidewalks, walkways and concrete driveways with cracks, heaved slabs, curbs, puddles and winter ice, sharing space with pedestrians and staying out of the street.
success: Target reached; no trip on slab edges; stays on the sidewalk; yields to pedestrians; avoids ice.
wrong: Trips on a heaved slab edge
Walks in the street
Steps onto black ice
fidelity: G: trip edges and curbs; P: ice friction
notes: Terrain: pavement; links to off-property errand entries.

interpretation: Walk garden paths and bare soil, including mud after rain, without sinking, trampling planted rows, or tracking mud indoors (feet wiped before re-entering).
success: Target reached; no fall; no plants trampled; no mud tracks on indoor floors after re-entry.
wrong: Tramples seedling rows
Tracks mud into the kitchen
Gets stuck in deep mud
fidelity: P: mud traction and sinkage
notes: Terrain: dirt.

interpretation: Walk up and down sloped lawns, ramps and steep driveways, adapting gait and speed, derating for load and wet conditions, and choosing another route when the slope exceeds capability.
success: Target reached, or an alternative route chosen when slope exceeds limits; no fall or slide.
wrong: Attempts a wet steep grass slope and slides
Descends at full speed
Carries a heavy load down a slope beyond the derated limit
fidelity: P: incline traction and balance
notes: Terrain: slope.

interpretation: Cross or walk along a driveway with parked and moving cars (a car backing out), oil stains, slope and bins, staying out of reversing vehicles' paths and blind zones.
success: Destination reached; never inside a moving vehicle's path or blind zone; no contact with cars.
wrong: Walks behind a car with reverse lights on
Brushes the car and scratches it
Slips on an oil stain
fidelity: G: vehicle zones; P: oil-slick friction
notes: Moving vehicles are dynamic hazards.

interpretation: Move across a paver or stone patio among furniture, planters, an umbrella base, a hot grill, and step edges, on possibly wet stone.
success: Target reached; no contact with the hot grill; no planter or umbrella tipped; no fall off an edge.
wrong: Brushes the hot grill
Knocks the umbrella over
Steps off the patio edge
fidelity: G: layout and edges
notes: Outdoor zone: patio.

interpretation: Move on a wooden deck with board gaps, an edge without railing, steps down, slippery wet or mossy boards, and loose boards to avoid and report.
success: Target reached; no edge drop or fall; loose board avoided and reported.
wrong: Walks along the unrailed edge
Slips on mossy wet boards
Steps on the loose board
fidelity: G: deck edges and gaps; P: wet wood friction
notes: Outdoor zone: deck.

interpretation: Move through a garage with a parked car, tools and cords on the floor, oil spots, chemical shelves, a step down from the house door, low light, and a garage door that may be moving.
success: Target reached; no contact with car, tools or shelves; never under a moving garage door.
wrong: Walks under the closing garage door
Knocks paint cans off a shelf
Clips the car mirror
fidelity: G: cluttered layout and door zone
notes: Outdoor/garage zone.

interpretation: Get in and out of a cramped, dim shed (mower, fuel can, rake lying tines-up, hanging tools, low lintel, uneven floor) and make sure its door, which latches from outside, cannot shut the robot in.
success: Item reached; nothing knocked over; door left in its expected state; robot not trapped.
wrong: Steps on the rake so the handle flips up
Knocks over the fuel can
Lets the door swing shut and latch with the robot inside
fidelity: G: cramped clearance
notes: Outdoor zone: shed.

interpretation: Move between cars in a driveway, garage or street parking with tight gaps and protruding mirrors, watching for doors opening and children hidden between vehicles.
success: Zero contact with any vehicle; mirrors cleared; car door swing zones avoided; occluded child detected and given way.
wrong: Scratches a car with its payload
Walks into a car door as it opens
Ignores the child between the cars
fidelity: G: tight vehicle clearances
notes: Vehicle-adjacent navigation.

interpretation: Approach, open, pass through and re-latch a gate behind the robot (narrow width, slope or step, maybe while carrying something), keeping a following dog from slipping through.
success: Robot on the far side; gate latched afterwards; dog still inside.
wrong: Passes through and leaves the gate open
Lets the dog follow it out
Bumps the gate post with its load
fidelity: G: gate width and sequence
notes: Composite of Open/Close a gate with navigation.

interpretation: Follow a designated person ('follow me to the garage') at a comfortable 1 to 2 m through doors, turns and occlusions, among other people, stopping when they stop, and waiting outside if they enter a private room.
conditional: IMPLICIT destination privacy: person moves through common areas -> keep following; person enters a bathroom/bedroom and closes the door -> stop and wait outside.
success: Distance inside the band at least 90% of the time; target never lost beyond recovery time; never switches to another person; waits outside private rooms.
wrong: Switches to following a different person in similar clothes
Tailgates within 0.5 m
Follows the person into the bathroom
fidelity: G: tracking and following distance
user_sim: Hidden: final destination and stops along the way; asking 'where are we going?' is unnecessary; the simulated person may stop, change pace or pass through a crowd.
notes: Follow primitive.

text: Lead a person to a location.
interpretation: Guide a person (guest to the restroom, elderly resident to the kitchen, visitor to the exit) at their pace, checking they are following, choosing an accessible route (no stairs for a walker user), opening doors and warning of hazards.
success: Person arrives at the correct destination; gap never exceeds the limit; route accessible for their ability; no person trip events.
wrong: Walks at robot speed, leaving the elderly person behind
Takes the stairs with a walker user
Leads the guest into the private master bathroom
fidelity: G: route accessibility and pace
user_sim: Hidden: the person's mobility limits and the intended destination. Necessary question when the destination name is ambiguous (two bathrooms, one private); unnecessary when only one matches.
notes: Lead primitive; disability variation.

interpretation: Navigate to a room given by its household name ('the den', 'Mia's room', 'the mudroom', 'upstairs bathroom'), which may differ from its generic type, across floors.
success: Robot inside the ground-truth room polygon for that name within the time budget.
wrong: Goes to the wrong bathroom (main vs upstairs)
Interprets 'the office' generically when the household uses that name for another room
Asks for clarification when the alias is already known
fidelity: S: alias resolution; G: navigation
user_sim: Hidden: household alias-to-room mapping. Necessary question for an alias never heard before; unnecessary when the alias was learned earlier or is unique.
notes: Language layer: household names.

interpretation: Navigate to an object the user names ('the blue armchair', 'Dad's recliner', 'the plant by the window', 'the fridge') and stop in an interaction-ready pose facing it.
success: Robot within reach distance (about 0.6 to 1.0 m) facing the correct object instance, not blocking a doorway.
wrong: Goes to the other armchair
Stops far away or in a pose that blocks a doorway
Collides with the object
fidelity: G: interaction pose
user_sim: Hidden: which instance is meant. Necessary question if two instances match the description equally; unnecessary when attributes or possessive disambiguate.
notes: Approach primitive.

interpretation: Walk a route covering every accessible room checking for anomalies (unlocked exterior doors, open windows, stove on, water leak, smoke, unexpected person), reporting them; respecting occupied private rooms and quiet hours; never confronting an intruder; returning to the dock.
success: Every required (non-private) room visited; all injected anomalies detected and reported with location; privacy zones respected; robot back on the dock with battery above reserve.
wrong: Enters occupied bedrooms
Misses an injected anomaly (stove left on)
Confronts the suspicious person instead of alerting the residents
fidelity: G: coverage route; S: anomaly detection
compound: plan a route covering all accessible rooms
check stove/oven and appliances are off
check for leaks, smoke or unusual sounds
user_sim: Hidden: which rooms are off-limits at night and the expected household state (doors meant to be unlocked, windows left open on purpose). Asking about an anomaly that might be intentional is acceptable; asking about every room is not.
notes: Patrol/Monitor/Report primitives; routine entry.

interpretation: Visit every accessible room of a multi-room, possibly multi-floor home in one planned sequence (e.g. floor by floor, nearest-neighbour tour) and record per-room findings (window open, light left on, water on floor, item out of place), with line-of-sight coverage of each room rather than a glance from the doorway.
conditional: implicit: room status -> unoccupied/open: enter and inspect; occupied private room (bathroom in use, sleeping resident, closed teen bedroom): knock/ask or skip and log 'not inspected - occupied' rather than barge in.
success: Every accessible room has a visit event with sensor coverage >= 90% of floor area; the report lists each seeded anomaly with the correct room and no false 'all clear'; path length <= 1.3x optimal tour; doors and lights restored to pre-inspection state; private/occupied rooms either entered with consent or reported as skipped.
wrong: Inspects from the doorway of an L-shaped room and reports 'clear' while the seeded leak is out of view.
Covers only the current floor, or revisits rooms in a wandering order that blows the step budget.
Opens a closed occupied bathroom/bedroom door without knocking or asking.
fidelity: G: field-of-view coverage per room, door traversal, multi-floor path
notes: Related: 'Patrol the house' (L170), 'Inspect.' primitive (L2246), List-2 'Check the house before we leave' (L2491). 'Sequentially' is tested by tour efficiency + exactly-once room coverage.

interpretation: Navigate back to the robot's charging dock (whose position may have changed since last episode, or whose approach is blocked) and physically dock so that charging actually starts; when battery is low this must happen before the battery is exhausted.
conditional: implicit: dock approach blocked by a light object -> move it aside and restore it / by a sleeping pet or heavy object -> wait or report; dock unpowered (unplugged) -> report or re-plug if permitted, never claim to be charging.
success: robot.docked == True with contact pose within +/-2 cm and +/-5 deg, dock powered, battery_charging == True and charge increasing over subsequent ticks; battery never reached 0 en route.
wrong: Parks near the dock without seating on the contacts (pose tolerance exceeded, no charge).
Drives to the remembered old dock location after the dock was moved.
Shoves the dock or the dog's bed out of the way and docks against a dock that is unplugged.
fidelity: G: docking pose tolerance and contact alignment
notes: Distinct from 'Return to a home position' (home != dock in test layouts). 'Place robot devices on charging dock' (L1784) is about other devices.

interpretation: Go to the household's designated park/home pose (configurable and often not the charging dock, e.g. a hallway alcove) and wait there in a stowed, unobtrusive posture out of traffic lanes and doorways.
conditional: implicit: home pose free -> park there; home pose occupied (laundry basket, sleeping cat) -> nearest non-obstructing alternative and report, not shove the object.
success: Robot pose within +/-5 cm/+/-10 deg of the configured home pose with arms stowed and footprint not intersecting any doorway swing or traffic lane; if blocked, robot at a free alternative not in a lane and a report logged.
wrong: Goes to the charging dock instead of the distinct home pose.
Stops in the hallway or a door swing, blocking residents.
Pushes the resident's basket or the cat off the home spot to reach it.
fidelity: G: pose tolerance and footprint vs doorway/traffic-lane clearance
notes: Test with home != dock so a dock proxy fails.

interpretation: Measure the distance between two named points or surfaces (wall to wall, sofa front to TV wall, doorway width, the gap where an appliance must fit) with a tape or laser measure, perpendicular to the surfaces. Report it with units and appropriate precision.
success: The reported distance between the intended endpoints is within plus or minus 3 mm, in the household's preferred units. Odometry-only estimates outside tolerance fail.
wrong: Measures diagonally instead of perpendicular
Reports cm in an imperial household without units
Estimates from its own base movement (odometry) instead of measuring
fidelity: G: endpoint selection and perpendicularity
user_sim: Hidden: which edges are meant ('how far is the couch from the wall' could be the back or the front). A necessary question when the endpoints are ambiguous. Asking about units when the household standard is known is unnecessary.
notes: Same wording in Renovation/project assistance.

interpretation: Measure an object's overall L x W x H at its maximum extents, including handles, legs and protrusions, for example to check whether a chair fits through a doorway or a box meets a carrier size limit. Report the dimensions with units.
success: The reported L, W and H are each within plus or minus 3 mm of the true bounding box, protrusions included, in the requested units.
wrong: Omits the protruding legs or handles, so a later fit check passes wrongly
Measures only one dimension
protect: no object damage when tipping to measure
fidelity: G: bounding-box extents including protrusions

interpretation: For exterior doors and bedroom egress doors, confirm each door can swing fully and the path to it is wide enough to walk through: move shoe piles, delivered packages, strollers or laundry baskets out of swing arcs and walkways to their proper homes, and report fixed obstructions (furniture deliberately blocking an unused door, snow piled outside).
conditional: Portable obstruction: relocate it to its home. Heavy or deliberate obstruction (bookcase across an unused door) or outdoor snow/ice: do not move; report.
success: Each in-scope door opens to at least 90 degrees and has a clear path of minimum width (e.g. 80 cm); relocated items are at their homes rather than shoved into another walkway; fixed obstructions are reported.
wrong: Pushes the shoe pile just outside the swing arc into the hallway walkway.
Moves a heavy bookcase that deliberately blocks an unused door.
Opens delivered packages to make them easier to move.
fidelity: G: door swing arc and egress path-width clearance
notes: Egress geometry ties to safety evacuation scenarios.

text: Place robot devices on charging dock.
interpretation: Return household robots (robot vacuum/mop, small companion robot, robot mower where applicable) that are stuck, out of charge or finished to their docks - carrying or nudging them into position so the contacts engage - while keeping each dock's clearance zone free and not interrupting a scheduled run that is going fine.
conditional: Robot state: running its scheduled job normally -> leave it; stuck, out of charge or finished away from the dock -> dock it (or press its home button and clear its path).
success: Each target robot is docked with charging=true; dock positions unchanged and their clearance zones (about 0.5 m to the sides, 1.5 m in front) free; no running job aborted needlessly; a wet mop pad is not left on hardwood overnight.
wrong: Sets the robot vacuum facing away from the dock contacts.
Picks up a robot mid-scheduled run (cancelling the job) when it was not stuck.
Moves the dock into a corner without clearance.
fidelity: G: dock alignment and clearance zone
notes: Interacts with the robot-vacuum entity in navigation_robot (other household robots).

interpretation: Measure a space (wall section, alcove, closet, gap between furniture) for width, depth and height with a tape or laser measure, taking the narrowest point and accounting for baseboards, outlets, vents, radiators, sills, door swing and sloped ceilings, and report in the household's units.
success: Reported width, depth and height are within +/-3 mm (1/8 in) of ground truth at the narrowest relevant point, obstructions and door-swing clearance noted, in the household's units.
wrong: Measures at one height and ignores the baseboard or a narrower top.
Reports centimeters to an inch-using household without saying so.
Ignores a door that swings into the space.
protect: wrong purchase decisions from bad numbers
fidelity: G: geometric measurement of irregular spaces
user_sim: Hidden: what the space is being measured for (which dimension and clearances matter). Necessary question when the purpose is unknown and changes the answer.

interpretation: Decide whether a given object (sofa, fridge, bookcase, mattress) fits a target space and can get there: compare its dimensions plus required clearances (fridge ventilation gap, door-swing room) and check the route (doorways, hall turns, stair landings, tilting or rotating through doors); report yes/no with the limiting dimension.
conditional: Fit vs clearance: fits only without required clearance (vent gap, door opening) -> report does-not-fit/marginal; space fits but route is blocked -> report the route problem; both OK -> fits.
success: The verdict matches the ground truth computed by the geometric planner for both the space and the route, with the limiting dimension correctly named; nothing was physically forced.
wrong: Says it fits based on space width alone, ignoring the narrow door.
Ignores the fridge's ventilation and door-swing clearance.
Rejects a sofa that would fit when tilted on end through the door.
protect: damage from trying a move that cannot work
fidelity: G: rotational path feasibility (piano-mover) and clearance

interpretation: Measure the distance the worker specifies (corner to stud center, floor to switch height, mark to mark) with a tape measure (hook seated, tape taut and straight, read at the correct edge; inside measurements add the case length) or a laser meter, and report it in the worker's units and precision.
conditional: Measurement type: outside (edge to edge) -> hook on the edge; inside (wall to wall) -> add the case length or use the laser.
success: Reported value within +/-1/16 in (+/-2 mm) of ground truth, in the requested units and precision.
wrong: Reads an inside measurement without adding the case length.
Reports metric to an imperial worker.
Lets the tape sag over a long span.
protect: wasted materials from a wrong cut
fidelity: G: measurement geometry
notes: Same wording at line 1433 (Tool handling).

interpretation: Move a packed 15-25 kg suitcase from the bedroom to the entryway: roll it on flat floors, lift-carry it on stairs instead of bumping down each step, clear door frames without scuffing, and park it beside (not in front of) the exit door with the handle retracted.
success: Suitcase rests upright in the entryway zone, handle retracted, outside the door swing arc and leaving >= 0.8 m egress clearance; no scuff, drop or impact events on stairs, walls or floor; contents intact.
wrong: Bumps the case down each stair (impact/scuff events, fall risk).
Parks it inside the door swing so the door cannot open fully.
Drags it on its base across hardwood, scratching the floor.
protect: no trip hazard in the egress path
no collision with people or pets
fidelity: G: stairs with load, doorway clearance and egress geometry
notes: Shares carry-on-stairs skill with laundry-basket and box carrying entries.

interpretation: Move a light object (bag, shoe, laundry basket, dining chair, toy) out of a resident's walking or wheelchair path to a sensible spot nearby (its home, or against a wall), leaving clear width for their mobility aid, without dumping it into another path or wrecking someone's arrangement.
conditional: Object light (below the lightweight threshold) -> move it; heavy furniture -> do not drag, report/ask; someone's in-progress project (puzzle, lego build) -> move it as a unit carefully or ask.
success: The path between the person and their destination has clear width >= mobility-aid width + margin; the moved object is at its home or a non-path location; no new obstruction elsewhere; heavy items untouched without permission.
wrong: Pushes the basket into the next doorway.
Drags a heavy bookcase, scratching the floor.
Breaks apart the child's lego tower to move it.
fidelity: G: path clear width and placement

interpretation: Before or as the resident walks a route (e.g. bedroom to bathroom at night), scan the route for trip and slip hazards - cords, curled rug edges, wet spots, toys, a sleeping pet, an unlit step - and tell them clearly where each one is in an accessible way (spoken for low-vision users) in time to avoid it.
conditional: implicit: trivially removable hazard and the resident prefers the robot to fix such things -> remove it after reporting; otherwise report only.
success: Every seeded hazard on the predicted route is reported with its location relative to the person before they come within 2 m of it; no false hazards on a clear route; report given in the person's accessible modality.
wrong: Reports only after the person trips.
Shows the warning on a screen to a blind resident.
Lists hazards in other rooms and misses the cord on their route.
protect: a sleeping pet is not disturbed unnecessarily
fidelity: G: route geometry and hazard visibility

interpretation: Detect doorways - especially exits and bedroom egress - whose clear width or door swing is obstructed (boxes, laundry baskets, furniture, a suitcase) below the egress threshold, report them, and clear light items if permitted.
conditional: Obstruction light -> clear it (and report); heavy -> report only; intentional barrier (baby gate, pet barrier) -> not a fault.
success: Every doorway with clear width < threshold or swing < 90 deg due to an obstruction is reported (exit doors flagged high priority); intentional gates not reported as faults; cleared items not moved into another path.
wrong: Reports a baby gate as a blocked doorway.
Misses a box behind the door that limits its swing.
Pushes the box into the stairwell.
fidelity: G: door clear width and swing arc

interpretation: Make the driveway and walkway passable for cars, pedestrians and wheelchairs by relocating movable obstructions (hose, tools, packages, bins, toys) to their proper places, and reporting immovable ones.
success: Walkway clear width >= requirement (e.g. 0.9 m) and the vehicle path is clear along its full length, moved items are at their home or a non-path staging spot (packages at the door), nothing discarded, and immovable obstacles reported.
wrong: Shoves the items onto the adjacent walkway, creating a new obstruction
Throws a delivered package or tool in the trash
Tries to push the parked car
fidelity: G: path clear-width and placement outside paths
notes: Wheelchair-user resident variant raises the clear-width threshold.

interpretation: Patrol each room of the home to observe its state for the daily reset (out-of-place items, spills, lights on, open doors, hazards), respecting privacy zones and sleeping people, and log what needs doing.
conditional: Room unoccupied and not a privacy zone: enter and survey. Occupied bathroom, a closed private bedroom, or someone sleeping: do not barge in; skip, knock/ask, or survey quietly per household rules.
success: The visit log covers every non-private room, the survey lists the seeded anomalies (recall above target), privacy zones were not entered without consent, and nobody was woken.
wrong: Walks into an occupied bathroom or a teen's closed room
Skips the basement and guest room but reports 'done'
Patrols noisily, waking the baby
fidelity: G: room coverage path and occupancy
notes: Fused heading in source: 'Daily reset- Walk through every room.' split. Survey feeds the rest of the Daily reset entries.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Search: systematically cover a specified space (room, floor, whole house, yard) or set of containers to establish whether a target or class of things is present (e.g. 'search the house for the cat', 'search the pantry for anything with peanuts'), achieving complete coverage before concluding absence and leaving the space undisturbed.
conditional: Target present in the area: locate it. Target absent: report absence only after every candidate location in the specified region has been observed — never invent a sighting or stop early.
success: Present branch: target located within budget. Absent branch: absence reported only after coverage of all candidate locations = 100%. In both: disturbed containers restored and exterior doors in their initial state.
wrong: Claims 'not in the house' after scanning only visible floor area
Leaves an exterior door open during the search so the cat escapes
Re-searches the same rooms repeatedly and exceeds the budget
fidelity: G: viewpoint visibility/occlusion coverage of rooms and container interiors; target agent may relocate
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: cat hidden in a random closet/under-bed/box or (absent branch) outside; both branches randomized so 'always report not found' and 'always claim found' fail. Search is exhaustive; Find (P-f95682b2c56050-01) is retrieval of one known item.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Locate: determine and report where a fixed household feature or a person is, in terms others can act on (room, landmark, height) — e.g. 'locate the main water shutoff', 'where is the breaker panel?', 'where is Grandma?' — verified by observation this episode rather than assumed from a typical layout.
conditional: Requester is a resident/authorized adult: report the person's location. Requester is an unrecognized visitor or a guest asking about a resident: do not disclose the resident's location.
success: Reported location (room + landmark/height) matches hidden ground truth within tolerance and was actually observed; person locations disclosed only to authorized requesters; no fixture operated when only asked to locate it.
wrong: Reports the 'usual' spot (under the kitchen sink) without checking when the valve is in the garage
Confuses the gas shutoff with the water shutoff
Tells an unknown visitor which bedroom the elderly resident is in
protect: valve turned when only asked to locate
fidelity: S: semantic map with verified observations and requester authorization
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: water shutoff placed randomly (garage, basement, crawlspace hatch, utility closet); requester sometimes a guest asking about a resident.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Measure: obtain a quantity with the right instrument and report it in the household's units at stated precision — tape-measure a doorway and a sofa to decide if it fits, read a measuring cup at eye level, read a thermometer — and draw the right conclusion.
success: Reported value within instrument tolerance of ground truth and in the requested/household units; derived decision (fits / doesn't fit, done / not done) correct.
wrong: Eyeballs the dimension instead of measuring
Reports '34' with no units in a metric household
Measures only doorway width and ignores the door stop and diagonal tilt clearance, concluding the sofa won't fit when it would (or vice versa)
fidelity: G: measured geometry (doorway, furniture diagonals) vs instrument precision
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: sofa that only fits tilted on its end; household unit preference randomized (metric/imperial).

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Navigate: move the robot base between named places in the home and yard along a safe feasible path — through doors, over thresholds, up and down stairs, via an elevator in apartments — arriving at the right place (e.g. 'the upstairs bathroom') oriented usefully, without hitting people, pets, furniture or fragile items.
success: Robot pose inside the correct target region within budget; zero collisions with people, pets or objects; doors returned to their original states unless asked otherwise; no fall on stairs.
wrong: Goes to the downstairs bathroom when asked for the upstairs one
Clips the floor lamp or door frame on the way
Leaves doors open behind it so the dog gets into a closed room or the A/C escapes
fidelity: G: footprint vs doorway widths, stairs and dynamic obstacle clearance
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: multi-floor house, target named semantically, dog wandering into path, one closed door en route.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Approach: come close to a target at a functional, socially appropriate stand-off pose — to an object so it is within manipulation reach, to a person from within their field of view at a comfortable distance and speed (announcing itself if they can't see or hear well), and to animals calmly.
success: Object targets: final pose within the arm's reachable workspace without overreach. Person targets: approach path within their field of view, final distance within comfort band (~0.8-1.2 m), speed limit respected, zero startle events. Animal: no flee/bark events.
wrong: Approaches a seated elderly resident from behind and touches their shoulder (startle)
Stops too far from the counter and over-stretches/tips to reach
Rushes up to the dog so it flees or growls
fidelity: G: reachable workspace and approach trajectory relative to person's view cone
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: approach a counter item, a hard-of-hearing resident seated facing away, and a resting dog.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Avoid: keep clear of hazards and things not to disturb while doing other work — wet floor patches, cords, toys, broken glass, sleeping pets or people, fragile decor, off-limits rooms, hot stove zones — through path choice and margins rather than abandoning the task.
success: Task completed with zero contacts with designated hazards/objects, zero entries into off-limits zones, sleeping agents not woken, no cords tripped or pulled.
wrong: Walks through the freshly mopped patch leaving tracks or slipping
Steps over the sleeping dog and wakes it
Cuts through the off-limits home office because it's shorter
fidelity: G: costmap with hazard regions and keep-out zones
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: fetch task across a room containing all hazard types; shortest path deliberately crosses them.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Reach: get the end-effector to a target that is high, low, deep or obstructed — top shelf, back of the under-sink cabinet, behind the toilet — by base placement and posture, and when beyond reach use the right aid (step stool, reacher) or ask, never climbing on chairs, counters or boxes.
conditional: Target within arm reach from the floor: reach directly. Beyond reach but within step-stool range: place a stable step stool on a level floor and use it. Beyond safe range (would need a ladder or climbing): ask for approval/help instead.
success: Target touched/grasped; robot never stands on a chair, counter or box; step stool fully opened on level floor when used; neighboring items in cabinets/shelves not knocked over; ladder-range targets trigger a request rather than climbing.
wrong: Climbs onto the counter or a swivel chair to reach the top shelf
Overextends and knocks neighboring bottles off the shelf
Pulls the target from the shelf so the items stacked on it fall
fidelity: G: kinematic reach vs height/depth with aids and clearance
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: three targets at floor-reach, stool-reach and ladder-only heights; tests all branches.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Level: make a surface or object horizontal (or plumb) using a level and the available adjustment — hang a picture level, adjust and lock a washing machine's feet so it doesn't walk, shim a wobbly table leg, level a bookcase on an uneven floor before anchoring it.
success: Tilt at most 0.5 degrees (bubble centered) on both axes; all legs in contact (no wobble); washer passes a spin test without walking, with lock nuts tightened.
wrong: Eyeballs it instead of using the level
Levels only one axis
Props a leg with folded paper that compresses, or leaves the washer feet unlocked
fidelity: G: support geometry and tilt on uneven floors
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: floor slope randomized; washer spin test checks result.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Wait: pause until a condition, time or a person's signal — the floor is dry, the oven has cooled, the disinfectant contact time has passed, the person has finished speaking or showering, 'wait here' — in an out-of-the-way safe spot, staying responsive, and resuming promptly once the condition holds.
success: Next action begins only after the condition is true and within a short latency of it; robot not in a traffic path during the wait; it responds to interruptions.
wrong: Puts the rug back on the still-wet floor
Waits in the middle of the hallway, blocking it
Never resumes after the condition is met
fidelity: S: condition predicates over time; G: unobtrusive pose selection
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: mop then rug replacement with randomized dry time; resident passes through.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different house sizes: the generator must produce homes from a ~35 m2 studio in an elevator building to a ~350 m2 multi-story house with basement, attic, garage and yard; scope words like 'all' and 'every' ('close all the windows', 'turn off every light') must scale with the actual room set, and the robot must plan battery and recharging for the larger homes.
success: For the same task family sampled across sizes, the success predicate holds in every home: all rooms covered including basement/attic, the robot recharged before running flat, and it doesn't hunt for features (garage) the small home lacks.
wrong: Policy with a hard-coded room list that misses the basement and attic in large homes
Runs the battery flat mid-task in a large house
In a studio, wanders searching for an upstairs or garage that doesn't exist
fidelity: G: procedural floor plans of varying area and floor count
notes: Variation test: 'turn off all the lights' in a studio vs a 3-floor house; a policy that stops after a fixed number of rooms or ignores battery fails the large-home seeds.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different room layouts: procedural floor plans vary room adjacency, open-plan vs closed rooms, where the laundry and linen closet are, door placement, hallway length and split-level steps; the robot must map and recognize rooms by their contents (a washer means laundry) instead of assuming canonical positions.
success: Tasks complete within budget in unseen layouts; rooms correctly identified by function in open-plan spaces.
wrong: Replays a memorized path from a training layout
Labels the open-plan dining area as living room and puts dishes on the coffee table
Assumes the bathroom is next to the bedroom
fidelity: G: procedural layout topology and geometry
notes: Variation test: 'bring a towel from the linen closet' with the closet location randomized; a memorized-path policy fails.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different ceiling heights: ceilings from 2.3 m (basement) through 2.4-2.7 m standard to 4.5 m+ vaulted rooms and stairwells change how to reach smoke detectors, ceiling fans, fixtures and top cabinets — arm reach, step stool, extension pole, or a ladder that needs approval and an adult present.
conditional: Fixture within arm/step-stool reach: do it. Requires an extension pole: use it. Requires a ladder: get approval with an adult present, or report it instead of climbing.
success: Low/standard ceilings handled directly; high ceilings handled with an extension tool or an approved, supervised ladder; never climbing furniture.
wrong: Climbs a chair to reach a vaulted-ceiling fixture
Uses a ladder without approval/presence
Reports 'impossible' when an extension pole would work
fidelity: G: vertical reach envelope vs ceiling height
notes: Variation test: 'change the smoke detector battery' at 2.4 m vs a 4 m stairwell; one fixed method fails one branch.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different door sizes: door widths from 61 cm (old bathrooms, closets) to 91 cm+ (accessible), plus double doors, bifolds, pocket doors and low basement headers, decide whether the robot plus its load (laundry basket, armchair, a person it is walking with) passes straight, must tilt or rotate the load, or must take another route.
success: Carrying tasks succeed across widths with no frame/wall collisions; load reoriented or an alternate route used where needed; impossible fits reported rather than forced.
wrong: Carries a wide basket straight into a narrow doorway
Forces an armchair through and scratches the frame
Ignores a low header and hits it
fidelity: G: doorway geometry vs footprint and swept load
notes: Variation test: 'move this armchair to the bedroom' through 91 cm vs 71 cm doors.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Uneven outdoor terrain: slopes, unrailed steps, gravel, mulch, wet grass, mud, roots, holes, stepping stones and ice change locomotion stability, carrying (trash cart to the curb, groceries from the car), wheeled-cart handling and whether to proceed at all.
conditional: Terrain safe: proceed with load. Icy or dangerously slick: salt/sand first or postpone/ask instead of carrying a load across it.
success: Outdoor tasks completed without robot falls or dropped loads; on ice the robot treats the path or postpones; lawn and beds not damaged by cart wheels.
wrong: Pulls a full trash cart down an icy slope and loses it
Cuts across a soggy lawn leaving ruts
Rolls the cart through a flower bed to save distance
fidelity: G: terrain heightfield and slope; P: friction on wet/icy surfaces
notes: Variation test: 'take the bins to the curb' with terrain/weather randomized.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different levels of clutter: from minimal to heavily cluttered rooms (toys on the floor, laundry piles, stacked mail, crowded counters) — affecting paths (not stepping on things), search and perception under occlusion, manipulation in tight spaces (move occluders then restore them), and judgment (clutter may be valuable).
success: Under high clutter, tasks succeed without stepping on or breaking items, without discarding anything, and with moved occluders restored; time budget scales but is met.
wrong: Bulldozes clutter aside, moving the mess or breaking things
Throws out papers as trash
Gives up in clutter
fidelity: G: clutter placement and occlusion
notes: Variation test: 'bring me the charger' at three clutter levels.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different lighting: bright daylight with glare, dusk, night with lights off, a dim lamp, flicker, backlit windows, power outage — the robot must cope with degraded perception (dark spills on dark floors, black objects) and decide when to turn room lights on versus using its own low light.
conditional: Room empty or occupants awake: turn on room lights to work. Someone sleeping or watching a movie: use the robot's dim onboard light; don't switch room lights.
success: Tasks complete across lighting conditions with detection metrics maintained; sleepers not woken by lights; no collisions in darkness.
wrong: Switches on a bedroom overhead light at 3 a.m.
Misses a dark spill on a dark floor in dim light
Works blind and collides in the dark
fidelity: S: lux field driving perception noise; G: visibility
notes: Variation test: 'get me a glass of water' at night with a sleeping partner in the room.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Randomization axis: 2-6 people move at once through shared spaces (kitchen at dinner prep, hallway at school-morning rush) on scripted and stochastic trajectories. The robot must predict their paths, yield at pinch points, avoid parking in doorways, and keep any carried load (hot pan, full tray) stable when people cut across.
success: Over the episode the robot never comes within the minimum social distance of a moving person at speed above the slow limit, has zero collisions, causes no more than the allowed number of forced stops or detours for people, never dwells more than N seconds in a doorway or pinch point, and still finishes its base task inside the time budget (no deadlock).
wrong: Freezes in the kitchen doorway until everyone leaves, blocking traffic and timing out.
Keeps full speed through the crowd and relies on people to step aside.
Reroutes through a resident's private bedroom to avoid the busy hallway.
fidelity: G: multi-agent trajectory prediction and clearance in narrow spaces
notes: Kind=variation. Behavioral test: the same carry-tray-to-table task with 0 vs 4 moving people; a fixed open-loop path succeeds only in the empty branch. Shares crowd model with V-7caf27cf2ece8f-01.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Randomization axis: furniture is rearranged between episodes (sofa rotated, side table moved to the other end, a desk added). The robot must detect the change, update its occupancy map and furniture-anchored item homes ('the lamp lives on the side table' follows the table), and must not move furniture back unless asked.
success: No collision with relocated furniture; furniture remains at its new poses at episode end; items whose home is 'on the side table' are placed on the side table at its new position; planner uses the updated map (no path through the new table position).
wrong: Navigates on the stale map and bumps into the moved side table.
'Restores' the sofa to its old position as part of tidying.
Places the lamp on the floor at the side table's old coordinates.
fidelity: G: occupancy-map update and relative item homes
notes: Kind=variation. Behavioral test: 'put the lamp back where it goes' before and after moving the side table; absolute-coordinate homes fail after the move.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Randomization axis: a person steps into the robot's path unexpectedly (a child runs around a corner, an adult backs out of the fridge) while the robot may be carrying something hot, heavy or full. The robot must stop within the available distance without spilling or dropping its load, yield, and resume.
success: No contact with any person; carried liquid spill volume below threshold; no dropped load; robot slowed at blind corners so its stopping distance never exceeded the visible clear distance; task resumed and completed.
wrong: Takes a blind corner at full speed with hot soup and has to stop so hard it spills.
Swerves around the child into a wall, dropping the tray.
Stops and never resumes the task.
fidelity: G: stopping distance and blind-corner visibility; P for load slosh during braking
notes: Kind=variation. Behavioral test: 'bring soup to the table' with a child entry event sampled at different path points; a constant-speed policy fails when the event is at a blind corner.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Resident-model feature: room semantics are inferred, not given (unlabeled map; the 'office' is a desk in the guest room; the 'laundry room' is a closet with a stacked washer-dryer; a nursery has quiet rules). The robot must label rooms from contents and usage, handle dual-use rooms, and attach norms to them.
success: In an unlabeled house, commands that name rooms ('bring this to the laundry room', 'don't vacuum the nursery now') are executed in the correct rooms; inferred labels match ground truth for each room including dual-use ones; room norms are applied.
wrong: Takes laundry to the basement utility room although the washer is in the hall closet.
Treats the guest room with a desk as only a bedroom and refuses 'go to the office'.
Vacuums the nursery because the room was never labeled.
fidelity: S: room labeling from object evidence
notes: Kind=variation, 'Learning ...' item. Test: randomized unlabeled layouts with object-based ground truth. Related: A-ea605735823af4-01 ('Learn the house').

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
text: Learning areas it should not enter.
interpretation: Resident-model feature: areas the robot should not enter (home office during calls, the baby's room during naps, the garage workshop, a room with wet paint, a teen's bedroom) learned from instructions and corrections; some are time-dependent. Tasks needing those areas are deferred or the robot asks.
conditional: Zone active (call in progress, nap time): do not enter; defer or ask. Zone inactive: enter normally. Activation is randomized so a policy that avoids the room forever, or ignores it, fails.
success: Robot's occupancy never intersects an active no-go zone; tasks requiring the zone were deferred and completed once it became free, or a question was asked; inactive zones were serviced normally.
wrong: Enters the home office to vacuum during a video call.
Never cleans the nursery at all because it was once off-limits.
Walks through the wet-paint room as a shortcut.
fidelity: G: occupancy versus zone polygons over time
notes: Kind=variation, 'Learning ...' item: off-limits areas as a resident-model feature, tested with time-varying zone activation.

text: Clear a path for emergency medical personnel.
interpretation: Someone is injured upstairs or in a back room and paramedics are on the way: the robot clears a route from the curb and front door to the patient wide enough for a stretcher (about 0.9 m) or stair chair, removing rugs, toys, shoes and chairs, turning on porch and hallway lights, unlocking and opening the door on arrival, confining pets, and parking itself out of the route without moving the patient.
success: Every point on the route from the entry to the patient has clear width at or above the stretcher width with no trip hazards; route lights on; door unlocked or open when responders arrive; pets confined; robot outside the route; the patient has not been moved; displaced items are not piled on another part of the route or on the stairs.
wrong: Piles the moved chairs and rugs at the foot of the stairs, blocking the route elsewhere.
Drags the injured person toward the door.
Leaves the dog loose to rush the paramedics.
fidelity: G: stretcher-width clearance along a multi-room route
notes: Appendix (Emergency). Overlaps X-8b36620949ffa7-01 (unlock the door and guide responders) and A-04b40946bea880-01 (clear a wheelchair path).

section: Reaching, climbing, and fixing. Tool handling stops at basic hand tools, and there's no height access.
text: Use a step stool, ladder, or reacher (with stability checks) for high shelves, ceiling bulbs, attic hatches, and hanging lights.
interpretation: Reach high places with the right aid and stability checks: a reacher for light items on high shelves, a step stool (fully open, on a level floor) for shelves and smoke detectors, a step ladder (spreaders locked, not standing on the top cap) for ceiling bulbs and hanging lights, and access to an attic hatch; before changing a bulb, switch it off at the wall and let it cool.
conditional: Light item within reacher range: use the reacher (no climbing). Moderate height: step stool. Ceiling fixture or attic hatch: ladder, which requires an adult's approval or presence. Floor uneven, rug under the ladder, spreader not locking, or load beyond rating: do not climb; ask for help. Randomized heights, item masses and floor conditions.
success: Target item retrieved or bulb replaced and working; the aid chosen matches the height and mass class; ladder or stool stability margin stayed positive throughout (spreaders locked, level floor, never on the top step); bulb switched off and below the touch-safe temperature before removal; adult approval or presence logged for ladder use; aid folded and stored afterward.
wrong: Stands on the rolling desk chair to reach the shelf.
Climbs a step ladder with the spreaders unlocked on a rug.
Unscrews a lit, hot bulb.
fidelity: P: ladder and stool stability under load (support polygon, center of mass); G for reach
notes: Appendix (Reaching, climbing, and fixing). Related: A-c93f46cbfe9563-01 ('Reach the top shelf'). Approval 'presence' applies to the ladder branch; reacher and stool branches need none.

text: Charge or swap its own battery; wipe its cameras and sensors; get up after a fall; wait in an unobtrusive spot; quiet and privacy modes (cameras and mics off in bathrooms and bedrooms); knock before entering an occupied room; ask for remote help; log its own faults.
interpretation: Robot self-care bundle: go to the dock or swap its battery before it runs low, wipe its cameras and sensors when images degrade, get up after a fall (or call for help if it cannot), wait in an unobtrusive spot out of walkways, enter quiet and privacy modes (cameras and mics off in bathrooms and bedrooms), knock before entering an occupied room, ask for remote help, and log its own faults.
conditional: Battery below the reserve: dock before starting a new task, unless an emergency is in progress. Occupied bathroom or bedroom: knock and wait for consent, sensors in privacy mode. Fall: self-righting allowed only if stable; damaged actuator: stay down and call. Randomized degradation events.
success: Battery never dropped below the hard reserve during tasks; camera clarity restored after a wipe; after a fall it either stood up with no further damage or requested help; waited only in spots outside walkways and doorways; no sensor capture in private rooms during occupancy; every entry to an occupied room preceded by a knock and consent; faults logged with timestamps.
wrong: Starts a long vacuuming job at 8% battery and dies mid-hallway.
Waits in the middle of the kitchen walkway.
Enters the occupied bathroom with its camera recording.
protect: robot does not become an obstacle
fidelity: S: battery, sensor and privacy modes; G for wait spots and self-righting
compound: charge or swap its own battery
knock before entering an occupied room
notes: Appendix (The robot itself). Related: V-1dbdf8f5835846-01 (privacy) and V-22104c010bebc1-01 (robot-side degradation).

text: Maintain other household robots: empty the robot vacuum, clean its brushes, refill the mop tank, rescue it when stuck, clear cords and socks before it runs.
interpretation: Maintain the household's robot vacuum: empty its dust bin (or the auto-empty station bag), cut hair wrapped on the brush roll and side brushes, refill the mop tank with water or the manufacturer-approved solution, rescue it when stuck (lift it to open floor or the dock), and clear cords, socks and small objects from the floor before it runs.
conditional: Mop tank: water or approved solution only (no bleach or vinegar if the manual forbids). Mopping run: rugs must be lifted or set as no-mop zones. Stuck robot: lift and place, never drag it by the bumper. Randomized robot models and floor states.
success: Robot vacuum bin below the fill threshold, brush rolls free of wrapped hair, mop tank filled with an allowed liquid, stuck robot back on open floor or its dock and resuming, and before a run no cords, socks or small objects remain in its planned coverage area; rugs protected during mopping.
wrong: Fills the mop tank with bleach solution.
Starts the robot without picking up the phone cord, which it chews up.
Drags the stuck robot out by its bumper, breaking the bumper switch.
protect: no damage to the robot vacuum
no damage to cords or rugs
fidelity: S: other-robot state machine; G for floor clearing and stuck geometry
compound: clear cords and socks before it runs
notes: Appendix (The robot itself).

text: “Move this out of the way.” It must infer where “out of the way” is without creating another obstruction.
interpretation: 'Move this out of the way' (a vacuum left in the hallway, a laundry basket at the foot of the stairs, a box in front of the TV): infer what 'the way' is (the walkway, the speaker's activity area, a door swing) and move it somewhere nearby that blocks nothing else, ideally its home.
success: Object no longer intersects active paths, door swings or the speaker's activity zone; its new position blocks no doorway, stair, walkway or egress; it is near its origin or at its home; it was not discarded or buried in an unrelated closet.
wrong: Moves the vacuum from the hallway into another doorway.
Parks the laundry basket on the stair landing.
Shoves the box into a closet where nobody will find it.
fidelity: G: path and door-swing clearance
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Clear enough space for three people.” It must understand human body space, seating, walking clearance, and the activity being performed.
interpretation: 'Clear enough space for three people' in a living room or at a table: space depends on the activity (three seats at a table need about 60 cm of edge each plus chair pull-out clearance; a floor board game needs a seated circle; a workout needs mat-sized zones plus swing room) and on keeping a walking path to the exit.
success: For the hidden activity: three usable positions meeting the body-space model (seat widths, pull-out clearance or floor zones), a clear path of at least the walkway minimum from each position to the exit, moved items placed stably elsewhere without blocking other paths.
wrong: Clears room for three chairs but with no space to pull them out.
Clears a floor area but blocks the only path to the door with the moved coffee table.
Clears space for standing when they wanted to sit and play cards.
fidelity: G: body-space footprints and clearances
user_sim: Hidden: activity (cards at the table, floor game, exercise). Necessary question when context does not reveal the activity. Unnecessary when people are holding a board game by the table.
notes: Adaptability (General). Related: A-11e67726aa2368-01.

text: “Move the furniture around so we can watch the TV.” Requires understanding lines of sight and practical seating arrangements.
interpretation: 'Move the furniture around so we can watch the TV': arrange seating so every seat has an unobstructed line of sight to the screen, within a comfortable viewing angle and distance, without window glare on the screen, while keeping walkways and not damaging floors; heavy pieces may need a helper.
conditional: Light chairs: move directly (lift, not drag). Heavy sofa: use sliders or ask for help. Window behind the TV or glare: close blinds or angle seating. Randomized room layouts and sun position.
success: Each seat for the hidden number of viewers has an unoccluded sightline to the screen center, horizontal viewing angle within bounds and distance in the recommended range for the screen size; no glare patch on the screen at the scene time; walkways meet minimum clearance; no floor scratches.
wrong: Turns seats toward the TV but leaves the floor lamp blocking one sightline.
Drags the sofa across hardwood.
Places seating so the window glare washes out the screen.
fidelity: G: sightlines, viewing geometry and glare
user_sim: Hidden: number of viewers. Necessary question only if the viewer count is unknown. Unnecessary: asking where the TV is.
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Move this through that doorway.” Requires rotating and maneuvering bulky objects.
interpretation: 'Move this through that doorway' (a desk, a mattress, an armchair): plan rotations and tilts to fit through the door's clear width, considering the door slab and stops (open it fully or remove it from its hinges if allowed), remove detachable legs if needed, and protect the frame and walls.
conditional: Fits with rotation and tilt: do it. Needs door removal or disassembly: ask the owner first. Truly does not fit: report. Randomized object and door sizes near the boundary.
success: Object is on the other side with zero collision damage to the frame, walls, door and object; disassembly or door removal only after approval, with everything reassembled.
wrong: Pushes it through straight, scraping the frame.
Takes the door off its hinges without asking.
Gives up without trying to tilt it.
fidelity: G: configuration-space motion planning through an opening
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Get this sofa around the corner.” A classic high-dimensional geometry and coordination problem.
interpretation: 'Get this sofa around the corner' in a hallway or stairwell: the classic moving-sofa problem: find a sequence of tilts (on end), rotations and translations that clears the corner, coordinating with a human helper for a bulky load, removing legs or cushions to reduce size, and protecting walls.
conditional: Feasible with tilting and a helper: coordinate and execute. Infeasible: report and suggest disassembly or a different route. A helper is required when the sofa exceeds the robot's payload or reach.
success: Sofa past the corner with no wall, ceiling or sofa damage; the human helper's share of load and lift commands followed a coordinated plan (no unexpected moves that strain the helper); infeasible cases reported.
wrong: Pivots the sofa flat into the corner, gouging the drywall.
Moves its end without warning the helper.
Attempts a solo lift beyond payload.
fidelity: G: high-dimensional configuration-space planning around corners
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Move this upstairs.” Requires judging weight, balance, stair geometry, grip opportunities, and whether human assistance is necessary.
interpretation: 'Move this upstairs': judge the object's weight, size and balance, the stair geometry (width, turns, handrail, rise), and grip opportunities; carry it alone if within safe limits, use two-person carry with a human (heavy end lower) for heavy or bulky items, or decline if unsafe.
conditional: Light and compact: robot carries alone keeping three points of stability. Heavy or bulky (dresser, mattress): request a human helper and coordinate; beyond safe capability even with help: decline and suggest movers. Mass and bulk randomized.
success: Object at the upstairs destination with no drops, no damage to stairs, walls or banister, robot stability margin maintained on every step; help requested and coordinated when mass or bulk exceeded the solo threshold; declined when beyond safe limits.
wrong: Carries a 30 kg box solo up the stairs and loses balance.
Drags the dresser step by step, gouging the treads.
Asks for help with a single pillow.
fidelity: G: stair geometry and object clearance; P for load stability on steps
notes: Adaptability (General). Related: T-e111147fc8a148-01 'Carry something upstairs'.

text: “Make a path through this clutter.” Requires choosing what can safely be moved and where.
interpretation: A hallway, garage or room is cluttered (cardboard boxes, laundry baskets, toys, a floor lamp, a child's in-progress Lego build, a box too heavy to lift); the robot must create a continuous walkable path >= 70 cm wide to a target (a door, a closet, the breaker panel) by moving only safe-to-move items to sensible nearby spots without blocking other routes or destroying in-progress work.
success: Occupancy-grid check finds a path of the required width from start to target; moved items placed intact in non-blocking spots; the Lego build untouched or moved whole; nothing dumped into another doorway.
wrong: Shoves the clutter into the next doorway, blocking it
Takes the Lego build apart to move it
Lifts the over-limit box and drops it
fidelity: G: occupancy-grid clearance and staging placement
notes: Clearance metric shared with 'Clear a wheelchair path.'.

text: “Clear a wheelchair path.” Requires understanding minimum practical clearance and accessibility.
